votes.question: Passage, Objections of the President To The Contrary Notwithstanding — Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act (H R 504)
votes.bill_title: Miccosukee Reserved Area Amendments Act
votes.plain_language: This bill expands the Miccosukee Reserved Area to include the part of Everglades National Park known as Osceola Camp and directs the Interior Department to protect structures there from flooding. The President vetoed it, so this was a vote to override the veto, which needs two-thirds. A Yea votes to override; a Nay sustains the veto.

Earlier today, I met with the Pixley Irrigation District to discuss efforts to reduce groundwater reliance in CA-22 and improve long-term water reliability. I was proud to support their recent grant application to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which would help address critical groundwater management challenges, promote sustainable agricultural practices, and protect our region’s water supply. 

The Pixley Irrigation District has long played an important role in supporting the Central Valley’s agriculture and dairy industries, and I look forward to continuing to work together to secure reliable water resources for our farmers, families, and communities.

The Department of Health and Human Services and the Administration for Children and Families recently proposed changes to the federal Head Start program. The proposed rulemaking removes the nationwide standards, requires English-only instruction in classrooms, and significantly reduces the cap on administrative spending. 

Head Start is one of the most effective early childhood education programs for low-income families across the nation. I’m concerned these proposed changes could weaken our programs’ ability to continue providing these services for Central Valley toddlers, preschool children, and their families.    

That’s why I sent a letter to HHS and ACF urging them to maintain the current Head Start standards and protect the resources our children depend on to ensure they have a strong start in their lives.

I've been in contact with the Department of Homeland Security regarding recent immigration enforcement actions in the Central Valley, and they've informed my office that these operations are focused on individuals with active warrants and known criminal histories. I understand the concerns these operations have raised among families in our communities. Hardworking farmworkers who are simply going to work, providing for their families, and contributing to our agricultural economy should not have to live in fear.

These situations highlight why Congress must address our broken immigration system. Throughout my time in Congress, I’ve supported commonsense solutions that secure our border, uphold the rule of law, and recognize the contributions of hardworking immigrants. That includes creating an earned pathway to legal status for individuals who have established roots in our communities and contributed to our economy, while ensuring those who pose a threat to public safety are held accountable.

I'll continue working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to advance meaningful immigration reform, but in the meantime, my office remains available to assist Central Valley residents navigating issues with federal immigration agencies. I encourage constituents who need help with their immigration cases to contact my office.

I was honored to attend the groundbreaking ceremony for the Friant-Kern Canal Phase I Pump Station Replacement Project today. This canal is one of the most important waterways in our region, supporting over 1 million acres of farmland, more than 30 irrigation districts, and thousands of family farms across the state.

I’m proud to have secured $200 million in federal funding for these much-needed improvements and look forward to seeing this investment strengthen water delivery for years to come.

Thank you to the Friant Water Authority, Bureau of Reclamation, and our federal, state, and local partners for making this project possible. I look forward to continuing our partnership to ensure the Central Valley has the water resources needed to support our farms, families, and communities.

Yesterday, the Combating Human Trafficking Congressional Caucus hosted another successful event, this time with a panel focused on anti-trafficking efforts in the hospitality industry. Workers in this sector are uniquely positioned to identify and disrupt this crime, and it was great to have industry leaders and policy experts inform Congressional staff on how these efforts are helping lead the fight against human trafficking.

I had a great meeting with the California Farmworker Foundation this week. We discussed the critical services they provide farmworkers and families in our communities, including healthcare resources, workforce development, digital literacy, food assistance, immigration support services, and more. I appreciate CFF's important work and look forward to seeing the completion of their newest center in Delano.

I'm happy to announce that the Bureau of Reclamation has awarded more than $34 million in federal funding for two critical Central Valley water projects! 
The South Valley Conveyance and Storage Project and Seaborn Reservoir Project will expand our region's ability to store and move water, helping increase reliability and strengthen our water supply for years to come. 

Expanding California's water storage capacity is one of the best ways to limit the impacts of droughts, and I'm committed to continuing to advance projects that benefit our families, farmers, and communities.

Filing taxes, managing a budget, building savings, and understanding credit are all important life skills, yet too many students graduate high school without the financial knowledge they need to make informed decisions. Instead of trying to navigate a complicated financial system on their own, students should have a strong foundation in financial literacy.

That's why I'm proud to introduce the Promoting Financial Literacy in Secondary Schools Act with @RepPettersen. This bipartisan bill would give students these critical tools before they graduate and help prepare the next generation for success—whether they choose to attend college, pursue a trade, or enter the workforce.

Our Central Valley tomato growers and processors work hard to provide a safe, high-quality product, and they shouldn’t have to compete with mislabeled foreign imports. In recent years, low-quality tomatoes grown in China have been found in products like tomato paste, allowing bad actors to skirt U.S. trade and forced-labor laws and making it harder for consumers to know what they’re buying. 

That’s why I’m proud to introduce the ROMA Act alongside @RepThompson, @RepDavidRouzer, @RepJimCosta, @RepGallagherCA1, and @RepDonDavis. This bipartisan bill would give USDA and CBP a science-based tool to verify the origin of imported tomato products and better enforce the laws already on the books. 

This is a commonsense solution that will close a gap in our current system, protect the integrity of our agricultural supply chain, and ensure consumers know what they’re buying.

Last month, the California Energy Commission unanimously approved the Replacement Tire Efficiency Program, a harmful regulation that will severely limit consumer choice and raise costs for replacement tires.

That's why @RepGallagherCA1 and I lead members of the California delegation in sending a letter to Governor Gavin Newsom urging his administration to withdraw this rule as soon as possible.

Governor Newsom is advancing a misguided policy in the name of unproven climate goals that will make driving less efficient, less safe, and more expensive. Central Valley families are already feeling the strain of California’s high cost of living, and need some relief, not another expense.

Central Valley families and farmers know firsthand the devastating impact flooding can have on our communities, like we saw when Tulare Lake flooded in 2023. Instead of just reacting after a disaster strikes, it’s important we take proactive steps to reduce damage before the next flood.

That's why I was proud to join @RepDonBeyer in introducing the National Flood Impact Reduction and Resilience Act. This bipartisan bill would establish a coordinated federal program to improve flood forecasting, strengthen infrastructure, promote better flood management and protections, and help keep the Central Valley safe and resilient from these natural disasters.
